title: AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) Access Log Parser
metaDescription: Debug and parse AWS ALB access logs. Generate verified Fluent Bit, Vector VRL, and Datadog Grok pipelines.
sampleLogs: https 2026-09-26T12:00:00.123456Z app/prod-alb/50dc6c495c0c9188 192.168.1.1:2817 10.0.0.1:80 0.001 0.002 0.000 200 200 287 403 "GET https://api.corp.internal:443/v1/health HTTP/1.1" "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64)" ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 TLSv1.2

https 2026-09-26T12:00:01.654321Z app/prod-alb/50dc6c495c0c9188 192.168.1.2:3412 10.0.0.2:80 0.002 0.015 0.001 500 500 120 184 "POST https://api.corp.internal:443/v1/checkout HTTP/1.1" "Stripe-Webhook/v1" ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 TLSv1.2

https 2026-09-26T12:00:02.998124Z app/prod-alb/50dc6c495c0c9188 172.16.0.45:49152 10.0.0.3:80 0.000 0.001 0.000 304 304 0 0 "GET https://api.corp.internal:443/static/app.js HTTP/2.0" "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X)" ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 TLSv1.3

fields.name: type
fields.description: Request protocol scheme (http, https, h2, ws, wss).

fields.name: elb
fields.description: Resource ID of the Application Load Balancer.

fields.name: client_ip
fields.description: IP address of the requesting client.

fields.name: target_ip
fields.description: IP address of the target container or EC2 instance.

fields.name: target_port
fields.description: Port of the target backend service.

fields.name: request_processing_time
fields.description: Seconds elapsed from ALB receiving request to sending to target.

fields.name: target_processing_time
fields.description: Seconds elapsed from ALB sending request to receiving header from target.

fields.name: response_processing_time
fields.description: Seconds elapsed from ALB receiving header to sending response to client.

fields.name: elb_status_code
fields.description: HTTP response code generated by ALB.

fields.name: target_status_code
fields.description: HTTP response code returned by target backend.

fields.name: method
fields.description: HTTP method verb (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE).

commonPitfalls: Target IP can be '-' if the ALB intercepted and responded directly (e.g. 403 or redirect). Use optional regex wrappers when handling direct ALB intercepts.
gRPC requests through ALB have special status codes; ensure elb_status_code parsing supports custom downstream error mappings.
HTTP/2 multiplexing may alter timing precision; ensure float parsers do not truncate microsecond precision.
productionTips: AWS ALB logs generate substantial volume in S3. Configure your Fluent Bit or Vector agent with an Amazon S3 SQS notification trigger to stream logs continuously rather than batch polling.

title: AWS CloudFront Standard CDN Access Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse AWS CloudFront CDN distribution access logs. Extract edge server locations, cache hit/miss statuses, and response latencies.
sampleLogs: 2026-09-26	14:22:15	IAD89-C1	1842	203.0.113.195	GET	d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net	/images/banner.webp	200	https://example.com/	Mozilla/5.0	-	-	Hit	e1W9dF4K3b7rT2v_Q==
2026-09-26	14:22:16	FRA56-P2	420	198.51.100.44	POST	d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net	/api/telemetry	204	https://example.com/checkout	curl/7.88.1	ref=checkout	-	Miss	z8X0aB5C9d1eF3g_L==
2026-09-26	14:22:17	NRT51-C2	9421	192.0.2.77	GET	d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net	/videos/preview.mp4	206	-	VLC/3.0.18	range=0-1024	-	RefreshHit	q2W3e4R5t6Y7u8I_O==

fields.name: bytes_sent
fields.description: Total bytes sent by CloudFront to the viewer.

fields.name: client_ip
fields.description: IP address of the client viewer.

fields.name: status
fields.description: HTTP status code sent to viewer.

fields.name: referrer
fields.description: HTTP Referer header value or hyphen.

fields.name: user_agent
fields.description: Client User-Agent header value or hyphen.

fields.name: query
fields.description: Query string portion of request or hyphen.

fields.name: edge_request_id
fields.description: Opaque unique CloudFront request trace ID.

commonPitfalls: CloudFront logs use tab delimiters (\t). Regex engines must preserve tab literals or handle \t escapes.
The first two lines of CloudFront log files in S3 are comment headers (#Version and #Fields); filter them before regex matching.
Fields with no value are recorded as hyphens (-). Use (?:%{TYPE}|-) to prevent parse failures.
productionTips: To monitor edge caching efficacy, calculate the ratio of edge_result_type == 'Hit' versus 'Miss' in real time using Vector VRL metrics aggregates.

title: AWS VPC Flow Log Parser (Default Format)
metaDescription: Extract IP protocol numbers, packets, bytes, and accept/reject decisions from AWS VPC Flow Logs.

fields.name: account_id
fields.description: AWS Account ID owning the ENI.

fields.name: packets
fields.description: Number of packets transferred during window.

fields.name: bytes
fields.description: Number of bytes transferred during window.

fields.name: start_time
fields.description: Unix epoch seconds marking capture window start.

fields.name: end_time
fields.description: Unix epoch seconds marking capture window end.

fields.name: action
fields.description: Security Group / NACL decision (ACCEPT or REJECT).

commonPitfalls: When no traffic occurs during the capture aggregation window, src_addr and dst_addr appear as hyphens with NODATA status.
Custom format VPC Flow Logs can append TCP flags and traffic path headers; ensure your parser matches your specific ENI format definition.
Ports for non-TCP/UDP protocols (like ICMP) are set to 0 or -1.
productionTips: High packet REJECT rates on port 22 or 3389 are prime indicators of external port scanning. Alert immediately in Datadog when action == 'REJECT' on sensitive ingress ports.

title: AWS CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format (EMF) Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse AWS CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format (EMF) structured JSON payloads to extract metrics and dimensions.
commonPitfalls: EMF logs must be valid JSON; unescaped quotation marks in nested payloads will break regex extraction.
CloudWatch natively extracts EMF, but external collectors (Fluent Bit) require JSON parsers to prevent redundant metric creation.
Timestamp is recorded in milliseconds, unlike standard Unix epoch seconds.
productionTips: Use Vector's native parse_json() transform when handling pure JSON logs for 5x higher parsing throughput than equivalent regex.

title: AWS WAF Access & Inspection Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse AWS WAF web ACL traffic logs. Monitor blocked requests, SQL injection signatures, and rate limit triggers.

fields.name: web_acl_id
fields.description: ARN of the terminating AWS WAF Web ACL.

fields.name: action
fields.description: Final rule action (ALLOW, BLOCK, COUNT, CAPTCHA).

fields.name: terminating_rule_id
fields.description: Rule or RuleGroup that triggered the action.

commonPitfalls: AWS WAF logs streamed to Kinesis Data Firehose are gzip-compressed JSON records by default; unpack before streaming to text parsers.
CAPTCHA and CHALLENGE actions contain transient client tokens that should not be stored in long-term plain text indexes.
IPv6 client addresses can contain variable-length compressed colons.
productionTips: Set up high-severity security notifications whenever the terminating_rule_id contains 'SQLi' or 'KnownBadInputs'.

title: Amazon S3 Server Access Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Amazon S3 bucket server access logs to audit bucket operations, data transfers, and anonymous requests.

fields.name: bucket_owner
fields.description: Canonical user ID of the source bucket owner.

fields.name: bucket
fields.description: The name of the target S3 bucket.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Date and time request was received in HTTPDATE format.

fields.name: remote_ip
fields.description: Internet Protocol address of the caller.

fields.name: requester
fields.description: IAM user ARN or canonical ID of requester, or '-' for unauthenticated.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description: String generated by S3 to uniquely identify request.

fields.name: error_code
fields.description: S3 error code (e.g. AccessDenied, NoSuchKey) or '-'.

fields.name: bytes_sent
fields.description: Number of bytes sent in response.

fields.name: object_size
fields.description: Total size of object in bytes.

fields.name: total_time
fields.description: Total milliseconds request took from first to last byte.

commonPitfalls: Key names containing spaces or special characters appear URL-encoded.
Anonymous requests show requester as a hyphen (-).
S3 log files can be delivered multiple times for the same time window; ensure your collector uses request_id for deduplication.
productionTips: To prevent logging loops, never configure an S3 bucket to output its own server access logs to itself.

title: AWS ECS FireLens & Fargate Container Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse AWS ECS container task logs with FireLens container metadata, task definitions, and log timestamps.
sampleLogs: [INFO] 2026-09-26T15:30:00.100Z container_id=c1a2b3c4d5e6 task_arn=arn:aws:ecs:us-east-1:123456789012:task/cluster/8899aabb message="Worker pool initialized with 8 threads"
[WARN] 2026-09-26T15:30:01.250Z container_id=c1a2b3c4d5e6 task_arn=arn:aws:ecs:us-east-1:123456789012:task/cluster/8899aabb message="Queue length threshold reached: 450 items pending"
[ERROR] 2026-09-26T15:30:02.900Z container_id=c1a2b3c4d5e6 task_arn=arn:aws:ecs:us-east-1:123456789012:task/cluster/8899aabb message="Database connection reset by peer (pool=orders)"
commonPitfalls: Fargate containers do not expose host EC2 metadata; rely solely on ECS task ARN and task revision.
Multiline stack traces can get fragmented across lines if Fluent Bit multiline parser is not explicitly configured on the container input.
productionTips: Use AWS FireLens with Fluent Bit to route container stdout directly to OpenSearch or Datadog, bypassing CloudWatch log ingestion costs.

title: AWS Lambda Execution & REPORT Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse AWS Lambda execution logs and REPORT metrics: duration, billed duration, memory size, and max memory used.
grokPattern: REPORT RequestId: %{UUID:request_id}\tDuration: %{NUMBER:duration_ms:float} ms\tBilled Duration: %{INT:billed_duration_ms:integer} ms\tMemory Size: %{INT:memory_size_mb:integer} MB\tMax Memory Used: %{INT:max_memory_used_mb:integer} MB
sampleLogs: REPORT RequestId: 4b294e77-1b03-4f9e-b9b5-44280df042e1	Duration: 85.42 ms	Billed Duration: 86 ms	Memory Size: 512 MB	Max Memory Used: 78 MB
REPORT RequestId: 8f12a344-9c88-4a11-82d3-112233445566	Duration: 1240.10 ms	Billed Duration: 1241 ms	Memory Size: 1024 MB	Max Memory Used: 320 MB
REPORT RequestId: d4e5f6a7-0011-2233-4455-66778899aabb	Duration: 12.05 ms	Billed Duration: 13 ms	Memory Size: 256 MB	Max Memory Used: 64 MB

fields.name: billed_duration_ms
fields.description: Execution duration rounded up to nearest 1ms billing bracket.

fields.name: memory_size_mb
fields.description: Configured function RAM allocation in MB.

fields.name: max_memory_used_mb
fields.description: Peak memory consumption reached by function.

commonPitfalls: Lambda REPORT lines are tab-separated; standard space-separated Grok expressions will fail.
Init Duration (cold start) only appears on cold invocations; make Init Duration optional in full pipeline rules.
productionTips: Calculate memory efficiency by computing max_memory_used_mb / memory_size_mb. Alert when usage exceeds 90% to avoid out-of-memory crashes.

title: AWS API Gateway Access & Execution Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse AWS API Gateway HTTP and REST API access logs. Extract API IDs, integration latencies, and authorizer responses.

fields.name: api_id
fields.description: AWS API Gateway API alphanumeric identifier.

fields.name: status
fields.description: HTTP response code returned to caller.

fields.name: response_latency
fields.description: Total latency in milliseconds from gateway to client.

fields.name: integration_latency
fields.description: Latency in milliseconds of backend Lambda or HTTP endpoint.

commonPitfalls: Custom authorizers that reject requests return 401 or 403 before integration_latency is populated; format can show '-' or 0.
AWS API Gateway supports custom JSON logging formats in CloudWatch; customize your pattern if using the JSON template.
productionTips: High disparity between response_latency and integration_latency indicates API Gateway throttling or authorizer bottleneck.

title: AWS Route 53 Public & VPC DNS Query Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse AWS Route 53 public and private DNS query logs to inspect resolver IPs, record types, and response codes.

fields.name: query_type
fields.description: DNS record type (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT).

fields.name: edge_location_ip
fields.description: IP of the recursive resolver that submitted the query.

commonPitfalls: Large numbers of NXDOMAIN queries from external resolvers indicate potential DNS tunneling or dictionary scanning.
Route 53 logs do not identify the individual end-user device, only the recursive DNS resolver.
productionTips: Stream Route 53 logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service to visualize global DNS query volumes and cache hit rates.

title: Kubernetes Nginx Ingress Controller Access Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Kubernetes Nginx Ingress logs with upstream responses, namespaces, and pod service endpoints.

fields.name: client_ip
fields.description: IP of client connecting to ingress.

fields.name: request_time
fields.description: Total request processing time in seconds.

fields.name: upstream_response_time
fields.description: Time spent waiting for backend pod.

fields.name: upstream_status
fields.description: HTTP status returned by backend pod.

commonPitfalls: If upstream fails or times out, upstream_addr can list multiple IPs comma-separated during retries.
Make sure request_time and upstream_response_time are cast to floats for latency percentiles (p95/p99).
productionTips: Monitor upstream_response_time versus request_time; high differences point to slow ingress network transfers or SSL handshake delays.

title: Apache HTTPD Standard Combined Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Apache HTTP Server Combined Log Format (NCSA combined) with client IP, timestamp, and user agents.

fields.name: auth
fields.description: HTTP basic authenticated user ID or '-'.

commonPitfalls: Bytes can be represented as '-' for 304 Not Modified responses; handle '-' or cast with fallback to 0.
Ident and auth are usually hyphens in modern web applications.
productionTips: Enable %D in Apache LogFormat to capture request duration in microseconds for latency analysis.

title: Caddy Web Server Structured JSON Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Caddy 2 structured JSON access logs with automatic TLS status, status codes, and duration float metrics.

fields.name: ts
fields.description: Unix epoch seconds with millisecond float.

commonPitfalls: Caddy 2 logs timestamps as decimal epoch seconds (e.g. 1695734400.123). Multiply by 1000 for milliseconds.
HTTP/3 protocol appears as 'HTTP/3.0' or 'h3'.
productionTips: Caddy's native JSON logging requires zero regex parsing overhead when using Vector's parse_json() transform.

title: Envoy Proxy Default Access Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Envoy Proxy access logs used across Istio service mesh and modern Kubernetes API gateways.

fields.name: response_flags
fields.description: Envoy flags (DC, UF, UT, UC, etc.).

commonPitfalls: When upstream connection fails, response_flags can be 'UC' (Upstream Connection failure) or 'UF' (Upstream Failure) and upstream_service_time is '-'.
Duration metrics in Envoy default to milliseconds, not seconds.
productionTips: Alert when response_flags != '-' as this indicates Envoy intercepted and terminated the request before the application responded.

title: Traefik Ingress Router Access Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Traefik Cloud Native proxy access logs with router names, service backends, and round-trip duration.
commonPitfalls: Traefik appends 'ms' directly to duration; ensure your pattern captures the integer before the 'ms' suffix.
Internal router matches show service_url as '-'.
productionTips: Use the router_name field to aggregate performance by Kubernetes IngressRoute resource.

title: Kong API Gateway Access Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Kong Enterprise API Gateway access logs with upstream routing latencies and consumer IDs.

fields.name: kong_latency
fields.description: Time spent in Kong gateway in milliseconds.

fields.name: upstream_latency
fields.description: Time spent in backend service in milliseconds.

commonPitfalls: Anonymous requests show consumer_id as '-'.
kong_latency represents plugin overhead; if this spikes, check custom Lua plugins.
productionTips: Calculate total round trip as kong_latency + upstream_latency to determine if performance issues are proxy or service related.

title: HAProxy Standard HTTP Access Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse HAProxy HTTP logs with frontend, backend, active server, connection queue timings, and termination state.

fields.name: tq
fields.description: Time to receive client request headers (ms).

fields.name: tc
fields.description: Time to establish connection with server (ms).

fields.name: tr
fields.description: Time to receive server response headers (ms).

commonPitfalls: The 5-timer slash string (tq/tw/tc/tr/tt) requires careful slash escaping in regex.
term_state flags (e.g. sH, cD, cR) explain whether client or server timed out first.
productionTips: tw > 0 indicates backend server starvation where incoming requests are queuing before being picked up.

title: Squid Web Proxy Native Access Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Squid caching forward proxy native log format with client cache results, MIME types, and peer addresses.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Unix epoch seconds with millisecond float.

commonPitfalls: Squid uses variable-width whitespace between fields; use \s+ instead of single space.
CONNECT requests for HTTPS tunnels will have '-' for MIME type.
productionTips: High TCP_MISS ratios for static asset domains signal Squid caching parameter tuning or cache directory exhaustion.

title: Nginx Standard Error Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Nginx error logs with pid, tid, client IP, server host, and upstream connection timeout messages.
sampleLogs: 2026/09/26 18:30:00 [error] 1240#1240: *4521 connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream, client: 198.51.100.4, server: api.example.com, request: "GET /v1/items HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/items"
2026/09/26 18:30:01 [warn] 1240#1240: *4522 an upstream response is buffered to a temporary file /var/cache/nginx/client_temp/0000000001 while reading upstream, client: 203.0.113.88
2026/09/26 18:30:02 [crit] 1240#1240: *4523 SSL_do_handshake() failed (SSL: error:0A000412:SSL routines::sslv3 alert bad certificate) while SSL handshaking, client: 192.0.2.99

fields.name: level
fields.description: Error severity level (debug, info, notice, warn, error, crit, alert, emerg).

commonPitfalls: The connection ID '*1234' only appears on events tied to client connections; daemon startup errors omit it.
Timestamp format uses YYYY/MM/DD, differing from Apache's DD/Mon/YYYY.
productionTips: Filter for [crit] and [emerg] levels in your SIEM to catch SSL cert expiration and out-of-worker-connections events immediately.

title: PostgreSQL Slow Query & Execution Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse PostgreSQL query execution logs. Extract query duration, user, database, and SQL statements.
sampleLogs: 2026-09-26 19:00:00.123 UTC [4821] app_user@production LOG:  duration: 452.120 ms  statement: SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = true ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50;
2026-09-26 19:00:01.450 UTC [4822] analyst@warehouse LOG:  duration: 12450.800 ms  statement: SELECT date_trunc('month', sale_time), sum(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY 1;
2026-09-26 19:00:02.900 UTC [4823] service@billing LOG:  duration: 89.400 ms  statement: UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 9410;
commonPitfalls: SQL statements can span multiple lines; ensure multiline aggregation is active on the file receiver.
PostgreSQL log_line_prefix can be customized; verify your prefix configuration matches.
productionTips: Normalize queries by stripping numeric literals and UUIDs into parameter placeholders before calculating aggregate query latency percentiles.

title: MySQL Server Diagnostic & Error Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse MySQL 8.0 server error logs with thread IDs, subsystem labels, and error codes.
sampleLogs: 2026-09-26T19:15:01.654321Z 12 [Warning] [MY-010055] [Server] IP address '198.51.100.4' could not be resolved: Name or service not known
2026-09-26T19:15:02.998124Z 45 [ERROR] [MY-010211] [InnoDB] Page [page id: space=4, page number=12] log sequence number 45892 is in the future

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp with microsecond precision.

fields.name: thread_id
fields.description: MySQL connection or background thread ID.

fields.name: label
fields.description: Log message priority (System, Warning, ERROR, Note).

commonPitfalls: Older MySQL 5.7 formats use short dates (YYMMDD) without ISO-8601 separators.
Thread ID is 0 for server internal initialization messages.
productionTips: Set up alerts on [ERROR] messages originating from the [InnoDB] or [Replication] subsystems.

title: MongoDB 4.4+ Structured Diagnostic JSON Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse MongoDB structured JSON logs. Extract command latency, namespace collections, and connection IDs.

fields.name: severity
fields.description: Severity code (F=Fatal, E=Error, W=Warning, I=Informational, D=Debug).

commonPitfalls: MongoDB 4.4+ migrated completely to JSON. Avoid applying legacy space-separated regexes to modern MongoDB clusters.
Slow queries append an 'attr' dictionary containing execution plan and docsExamined count.
productionTips: Filter for component == 'COMMAND' and id == 51803 to isolate slow query warnings.

title: Redis Slowlog & Execution Timer Parser
metaDescription: Parse Redis slow command logs to audit blocking operations like KEYS, HGETALL, or SMEMBERS.

fields.name: argument
fields.description: Primary command argument or key target.

commonPitfalls: Redis records slowlog durations in microseconds (us), not milliseconds.
Commands without arguments (like FLUSHDB or PING) will omit the argument element.
productionTips: Redis is single-threaded. Any command exceeding 10,000us (10ms) blocks all concurrent client requests; alert immediately on KEYS or HGETALL calls.

title: Apache Cassandra JVM System Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Apache Cassandra distributed database system logs with log levels, thread names, and Java classes.
sampleLogs: WARN  [Native-Transport-Requests-1] 2026-09-26 20:00:01,450 StorageProxy.java:2140 - Some replica queries for keyspace1 failed after timeout
ERROR [GossipStage:1] 2026-09-26 20:00:02,890 Gossiper.java:820 - Node 192.168.1.50 is now dead

fields.name: level
fields.description: Log4j logging level (INFO, WARN, ERROR, DEBUG).

fields.name: thread_name
fields.description: JVM thread name executing the task.

commonPitfalls: Cassandra timestamps use commas for fractional milliseconds (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,sss).
Thread names often contain colons, dashes, and numbers (e.g. CompactionExecutor:1).
productionTips: GossipStage ERROR events signal network partitions or crashed Cassandra nodes requiring automated cluster repair.

title: Elasticsearch & OpenSearch Cluster Node JSON Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Elasticsearch and OpenSearch cluster JSON logs. Extract node names, cluster state changes, and shard allocations.
commonPitfalls: Elasticsearch uses commas for millisecond offsets in timestamps.
Circuit breaker warnings indicate JVM heap pressure and imminent OutOfMemory errors.
productionTips: Track circuit breaker trigger frequency to scale Elasticsearch data node memory proactively.

title: ClickHouse Server Columnar DB Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse ClickHouse server logs. Audit background merge operations, parts mutations, and query threads.
sampleLogs: 2026.09.26 20:30:00.123456 [ 4821 ] { 7d8e9f0a-1122-3344-5566-778899aabbcc } <Information> executeQuery: (from 198.51.100.4:48210, user: default) SELECT count() FROM telemetry
2026.09.26 20:30:01.654321 [ 4822 ] { } <Information> MergeTreeBackgroundExecutor: Selected 12 parts from 202609 to merge

fields.name: query_id
fields.description: Distributed query UUID identifier or empty.

commonPitfalls: ClickHouse formats dates with periods (YYYY.MM.DD).
Background worker tasks (like merges) have an empty query_id '{ }'.
productionTips: Use the query_id field to join server log traces with the ClickHouse system.query_log table for end-to-end auditability.

title: CockroachDB Distributed SQL Audit Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse CockroachDB distributed SQL audit logs with node IDs, transaction states, and SQL queries.
sampleLogs: I260926 20:45:00.123456 1 sql/exec: [n1,client=198.51.100.4:48210,user=root] executed statement: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name STRING)
I260926 20:45:01.654321 2 sql/exec: [n2,client=203.0.113.88:51240,user=app] executed statement: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice')
I260926 20:45:02.998124 1 sql/exec: [n1,client=192.0.2.14:39100,user=root] executed statement: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE id = 1

fields.name: context
fields.description: Client IP and authenticated user details.

commonPitfalls: CockroachDB prefixes log lines with severity letters (I=Info, W=Warning, E=Error) concatenated directly to date.
Multiline transactions output sub-statements that must be grouped by client connection.
productionTips: Forward CockroachDB audit logs to non-repudiation cold storage for SOC2 / HIPAA compliance audits.

title: Kubernetes Containerd CRI Pod Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Kubernetes Containerd CRI runtime pod logs with ISO timestamps, stream types (stdout/stderr), and partial line markers.
sampleLogs: 2026-09-26T21:00:00.123456789Z stdout F [INFO] Application started successfully on port 8080
2026-09-26T21:00:01.456789012Z stderr F [ERROR] Failed to connect to Redis cache at redis.default.svc:6379
2026-09-26T21:00:02.789012345Z stdout P First chunk of a very long split log line that exceeded buffer...

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp with nanosecond precision.

fields.name: tag
fields.description: Line completion flag: 'F' (Full/Finished) or 'P' (Partial multiline split).

fields.name: log_message
fields.description: Raw log message output emitted by container.

commonPitfalls: Containerd splits lines exceeding 16KB into multiple lines tagged with 'P' (Partial). You must configure your collector to concatenate 'P' lines with the concluding 'F' line.
The tag field is always a single letter (F or P).
productionTips: In Fluent Bit, use the 'multiline.parser cri' filter to automatically reassemble fragmented 'P' lines into single log events.

title: Docker JSON-File Logging Driver Parser
metaDescription: Parse Docker daemon json-file container logs with log output, stream channels, and UTC timestamps.
commonPitfalls: Docker escapes newlines inside the 'log' JSON property as '\n'.
Large files can cause disk space starvation if log rotation (max-size, max-file) is not configured in daemon.json.
productionTips: Set max-size: '50m' and max-file: '5' in /etc/docker/daemon.json to prevent unchecked log growth.

title: Kubernetes Kube-APIServer Audit Event Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Kubernetes API audit logs to monitor RBAC operations, secret access, and pod creation events.

fields.name: level
fields.description: Audit event detail level (None, Metadata, Request, RequestResponse).

fields.name: verb
fields.description: API action (get, list, create, update, delete, watch).

fields.name: username
fields.description: Identity of user or ServiceAccount invoking the API.

commonPitfalls: Audit logs produce massive throughput. Apply strict audit policy filters to ignore frequent read-only events (e.g. node heartbeats).
Full RequestResponse level records contain entire YAML bodies and can exceed 100KB per event.
productionTips: Alert immediately on any unauthorized 'get' or 'list' attempts targeting the 'secrets' resource in any namespace.

title: CoreDNS Kubernetes Cluster DNS Query Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse CoreDNS logs in Kubernetes to monitor DNS resolution latencies, NXDOMAIN lookups, and pod service queries.

fields.name: flags
fields.description: DNS header response flags (qr, aa, rd, ra).

commonPitfalls: The duration is in seconds (e.g. 0.0002 = 200 microseconds). Multiply by 1000 for milliseconds.
High rates of AAAA lookups on cluster.local domains are typical for default Node.js and Alpine Linux DNS resolvers.
productionTips: High SERVFAIL responses from CoreDNS indicate upstream DNS provider timeouts or rate limiting by cloud providers (e.g. AWS Route 53 limits at 1024 packets/sec/ENI).

title: Kubernetes Kubelet Node Daemon Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Kubelet node daemon logs with system severity levels, source files, and container lifecycle events.
sampleLogs: I0926 21:45:00.123456 1420 kuberuntime_manager.go:450] Container 'app' in pod 'web-7d8e9f' started successfully
E0926 21:45:01.654321 1420 kubelet_pods.go:120] Failed to pull image 'registry.corp.internal/app:v2': ImagePullBackOff
W0926 21:45:02.998124 1420 eviction_manager.go:210] Node memory threshold crossed, initiating pod eviction

fields.name: severity
fields.description: Single-character severity: I=Info, W=Warning, E=Error, F=Fatal.

commonPitfalls: Kubelet uses standard Google klog formatting, where severity character precedes date without delimiter.
Fatal logs (F) trigger immediate kubelet termination.
productionTips: Alert on 'ImagePullBackOff' or 'eviction_manager' logs across nodes to preempt service outages.

title: Project Calico CNI Network Policy Audit Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Project Calico Kubernetes CNI flow logs to audit network policy drops and inter-pod communications.
grokPattern: %{TIMESTAMP_ISO8601:timestamp} %{NOTSPACE:hostname} %{NOTSPACE:cni}: \[%{WORD:action}\] IN=%{NOTSPACE:in_iface} OUT=%{NOTSPACE:out_iface} MAC=%{NOTSPACE:mac} SRC=%{IP:src_ip} DST=%{IP:dst_ip} PROTO=%{WORD:proto} SPT=%{INT:src_port:integer} DPT=%{INT:dst_port:integer}
sampleLogs: 2026-09-26T22:00:00.123Z node-1.corp.internal calico-packet: [DROP] IN=cali1234 OUT=eth0 MAC=00:11:22:33:44:55 SRC=10.244.1.45 DST=198.51.100.4 PROTO=TCP SPT=48210 DPT=443
2026-09-26T22:00:01.450Z node-2.corp.internal calico-packet: [ALLOW] IN=cali5678 OUT=cali9012 MAC=00:11:22:33:44:55 SRC=10.244.2.14 DST=10.244.2.80 PROTO=TCP SPT=51240 DPT=8080
2026-09-26T22:00:02.890Z node-1.corp.internal calico-packet: [DROP] IN=cali1234 OUT=eth0 MAC=00:11:22:33:44:55 SRC=10.244.1.45 DST=169.254.169.254 PROTO=TCP SPT=39100 DPT=80
commonPitfalls: Attempts to reach 169.254.169.254 (cloud instance metadata) that get dropped indicate pods attempting credential exfiltration.
ICMP packets omit SPT and DPT fields.
productionTips: Aggregate DROP actions by src_ip to locate compromised pods attempting lateral network traversal.

title: Kubernetes Cluster Event & OOMKilled Record Parser
metaDescription: Parse Kubernetes cluster event warnings, node pressure, OOMKilled triggers, and CrashLoopBackOff states.
sampleLogs: {"reason":"OOMKilled","message":"Container 'worker' in pod exceeded memory limit and was terminated","type":"Warning","involvedObject":{"kind":"Pod","name":"worker-5f6d7c","namespace":"default"}}

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Short machine-readable event code (OOMKilled, Scheduled, Unhealthy).

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Target Kubernetes resource type (Pod, Node, Deployment).

commonPitfalls: OOMKilled warnings are ephemeral; if you don't stream them off-cluster to Fluent Bit or Vector, they are purged after 1 hour.
Cluster event objects do not retain stack traces.
productionTips: Track reason == 'OOMKilled' metrics over time to right-size pod memory request and limit configurations.

title: Spring Boot Logback Standard & Multiline Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Spring Boot Java Logback application logs with timestamps, thread pools, log levels, and Java class names.
sampleLogs: 2026-09-26 22:15:00.120  INFO 1420 --- [nio-8080-exec-1] c.e.demo.controller.UserController       : Fetching user profile with id=9410
2026-09-26 22:15:01.450  WARN 1420 --- [nio-8080-exec-2] c.e.demo.service.PaymentService          : Retry attempt 2 for external gateway transaction tx_8819
2026-09-26 22:15:02.890 ERROR 1420 --- [nio-8080-exec-3] c.e.demo.exception.GlobalHandler         : NullPointerException occurred at OrderProcessor.java:84

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Local ISO-8601 timestamp with millisecond precision.

fields.name: logger
fields.description: Full package and Java class name.

commonPitfalls: Spring Boot uses variable whitespace padding (e.g. two spaces between timestamp and level); use \s+ instead of fixed spaces.
Java stack traces follow the initial message line; configure multiline collector rules anchored to the ISO-8601 timestamp.
productionTips: Configure Spring Boot to output JSON using Logstash-Logback-Encoder in production to eliminate all regex parsing costs.

title: Gunicorn Python WSGI Server Access Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Gunicorn Python WSGI access logs with response times, byte sizes, and HTTP methods.
commonPitfalls: Duration in Gunicorn (%L or %D) can be configured in either seconds or microseconds; verify your gunicorn.conf.py logging string.
Sync worker architectures stall when duration_seconds exceeds worker-timeout.
productionTips: Alert when duration_seconds exceeds 10.0 seconds to prevent Gunicorn master from killing silent worker processes.

title: Golang Logrus Structured JSON Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Golang Logrus structured JSON application logs with log levels, callers, and contextual fields.

fields.name: caller
fields.description: Go source code file and line number.

commonPitfalls: Custom WithFields() calls inject additional dynamic keys into the JSON root.
Caller reporting in Logrus incurs a slight CPU penalty via runtime.Caller().
productionTips: Use Go's native log/slog package in modern Go 1.21+ services for faster allocations than Logrus.

title: Django Python Web Framework Request Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Django framework request logs with HTTP status, handler views, and execution times.
commonPitfalls: 500 Internal Server Errors will append a Python traceback on subsequent lines.
CSRF token rejections produce 403 Forbidden with django.security logger.
productionTips: Capture 500 errors in Sentry alongside your log aggregation pipeline for instant stack frame inspection.

title: Node.js Bunyan Structured JSON Logger Parser
metaDescription: Parse Node.js Bunyan JSON logs with numeric severity levels, PIDs, hostnames, and event records.
commonPitfalls: Bunyan records level as an integer (e.g. 30 for INFO). Map numeric levels to standard strings in downstream collectors.
The 'err' object is serialized as a nested JSON structure when exceptions occur.
productionTips: Add a Vector VRL remap rule: `.level = if .level >= 50 { 'error' } else if .level >= 40 { 'warn' } else { 'info' }`.

title: Ruby on Rails Production Request Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Ruby on Rails production request headers, controllers, actions, and processing parameters.
commonPitfalls: Rails splits single requests across 4-6 lines (Processing by, Parameters, Completed). Use lograge gem to emit single-line JSON.
ActiveRecord query logs interlace between request start and completion lines.
productionTips: Install the 'lograge' gem in Rails to transform multi-line Rails logging into uniform single-line JSON events.

title: Rust Tracing-Subscriber JSON Event Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Rust tracing-subscriber structured JSON telemetry logs with spans, target modules, and fields.

fields.name: level
fields.description: Tracing level (TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR).

commonPitfalls: Custom fields attached to tracing spans appear as sibling keys inside the 'fields' dictionary.
Rust async task switches can emit interleaved events from multiple tasks.
productionTips: Use tracing-opentelemetry in Rust to export directly to OpenTelemetry Collector via gRPC rather than writing text logs to disk.

title: ASP.NET Core Kestrel Hosting Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse ASP.NET Core Kestrel hosting logs with event IDs, categories, and HTTP response codes.
sampleLogs: info: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics[1]      Request starting HTTP/1.1 GET http://localhost:5000/api/weather
info: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics[1]      Request starting HTTP/2.0 POST https://api.corp.internal/checkout
info: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics[1]      Request starting HTTP/1.1 GET http://localhost:5000/healthz
commonPitfalls: ASP.NET Core formats logs across multiple lines (Request starting, Request finished). Use Serilog to emit structured JSON.
Kestrel adds six spaces before 'Request starting'.
productionTips: Configure Serilog.AspNetCore to write directly to JSON format in production.

title: Syslog RFC 5424 Strict IETF Format Parser
metaDescription: Parse IETF RFC 5424 enterprise syslog headers, facility priority codes, hostnames, app names, and message payloads.
sampleLogs: <34>1 2026-09-26T22:14:15.003Z mymachine.example.com su 7704 ID47 [exampleSDID@32473 iut="3" eventSource="Application"] 'su root' failed for lonvick on /dev/pts/8
<165>1 2026-09-26T22:15:01.120Z webserver01.corp nginx 1420 ID12 - Worker process exited normally
<14>1 2026-09-26T22:16:45.990Z firewall02.corp sudo 8901 ID99 - admin : TTY=pts/0 ; PWD=/etc ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/bin/systemctl restart nginx

fields.name: structured_data
fields.description: Structured data elements inside brackets or '-'.

commonPitfalls: Structured data can be a hyphen (-) when no metadata is attached.
Priority calculation: Facility = priority / 8, Severity = priority % 8.
productionTips: Configure rsyslog or syslog-ng with TLS to ensure RFC 5424 logs are encrypted in transit across networks.

title: Syslog RFC 3164 Traditional BSD Format Parser
metaDescription: Parse traditional BSD RFC 3164 syslog entries with priority angles, month-day timestamps, and program tags.
sampleLogs: <34>Sep 26 22:14:15 server1 su[7704]: 'su root' failed for lonvick on /dev/pts/8
<165>Sep 26 22:15:01 web01 nginx[1420]: worker process exited normally
<13>Sep 26 22:16:45 router01 kernel: eth0: link up, 1000Mbps, full-duplex
commonPitfalls: RFC 3164 does not record the year in the timestamp; collectors must infer the current calendar year.
Process ID inside brackets is optional (e.g. kernel messages lack PID).
productionTips: Upgrade network devices to RFC 5424 to avoid year rollover ambiguity on December 31st.

title: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Firewall Traffic Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Palo Alto PAN-OS firewall CSV traffic logs to extract security zones, action verdicts, and threat classifications.
commonPitfalls: PAN-OS logs are comma-separated without spaces. Field positions vary slightly between PAN-OS 9.0, 10.0, and 11.0.
Dates use forward slashes (YYYY/MM/DD).
productionTips: Correlate rule_name and action to identify shadow rules that permit unwanted lateral movement.

title: Fortinet FortiGate UTM Key-Value Firewall Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Fortinet FortiGate UTM key-value firewall logs with VDOMs, policy IDs, and interface routing.
grokPattern: date=%{YEAR:year}-%{MONTHNUM:month}-%{MONTHDAY:day} time=%{TIME:time} devname="%{NOTSPACE:devname}" devid="%{NOTSPACE:devid}" type="%{WORD:type}" subtype="%{WORD:subtype}" level="%{WORD:level}" action="%{WORD:action}" srcip=%{IP:srcip} dstip=%{IP:dstip} srcport=%{INT:srcport:integer} dstport=%{INT:dstport:integer} proto=%{INT:proto:integer} policyid=%{INT:policyid:integer}
sampleLogs: date=2026-09-26 time=22:45:00 devname="FGT-EDGE-01" devid="FGT60D123456" type="traffic" subtype="forward" level="notice" action="accept" srcip=192.168.1.10 dstip=198.51.100.4 srcport=54210 dstport=443 proto=6 policyid=1

date=2026-09-26 time=22:45:01 devname="FGT-EDGE-01" devid="FGT60D123456" type="traffic" subtype="forward" level="warning" action="deny" srcip=10.0.1.15 dstip=203.0.113.88 srcport=48210 dstport=22 proto=6 policyid=2

date=2026-09-26 time=22:45:02 devname="FGT-EDGE-01" devid="FGT60D123456" type="traffic" subtype="forward" level="notice" action="accept" srcip=192.168.1.45 dstip=192.0.2.14 srcport=61240 dstport=53 proto=17 policyid=3
commonPitfalls: FortiGate outputs key=value pairs where some values are quoted (devname="...") while IP and ports are unquoted.
Key order is not guaranteed across FortiOS firmware updates.
productionTips: Use a dedicated key-value parser filter (like Fluent Bit's key_value or Vector's parse_key_value) for arbitrary FortiGate log streams.

title: Cisco ASA Adaptive Security Appliance Syslog Parser
metaDescription: Parse Cisco ASA firewall connection build and teardown syslog events with direction, protocol, and duration.
sampleLogs: 2026-09-26T23:00:00Z asa-core-01 : %ASA-6-302013: Built inbound TCP connection 12450 for outside:198.51.100.4/54210 to inside:10.0.1.10/443
2026-09-26T23:00:01Z asa-core-01 : %ASA-6-302013: Built outbound UDP connection 12451 for inside:10.0.1.45/61240 to outside:198.51.100.88/53
2026-09-26T23:00:02Z asa-core-02 : %ASA-6-302013: Built inbound TCP connection 12452 for outside:203.0.113.88/48210 to dmz:172.16.1.15/8080
commonPitfalls: Cisco ASA interfaces are suffixed directly before IP with a colon (e.g. outside:198.51.100.4).
Connection teardown logs (%ASA-6-302014) have different syntax including duration and bytes.
productionTips: Match connection IDs across 302013 (Built) and 302014 (Teardown) to compute exact session lifetime and data volume per flow.

title: Suricata IDS/IPS EVE JSON Alert Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Suricata Network Threat Detection EVE JSON logs with signature IDs, severity categories, and packet flows.
sampleLogs: {"timestamp":"2026-09-26T23:15:00.120Z","flow_id":12450889,"event_type":"alert","src_ip":"198.51.100.4","src_port":54210,"dest_ip":"10.0.1.10","dest_port":80,"proto":"TCP","alert":{"action":"allowed","gid":1,"signature_id":2100498,"signature":"GPL ATTACK_RESPONSE id check returned root","category":"Potentially Bad Traffic","severity":2}}

{"timestamp":"2026-09-26T23:15:01.450Z","flow_id":12450890,"event_type":"alert","src_ip":"203.0.113.88","src_port":48210,"dest_ip":"10.0.1.15","dest_port":443,"proto":"TCP","alert":{"action":"blocked","gid":1,"signature_id":2014520,"signature":"ET EXPLOIT Apache Struts RCE","category":"Attempted Administrator Privilege Gain","severity":1}}

{"timestamp":"2026-09-26T23:15:02.890Z","flow_id":12450891,"event_type":"alert","src_ip":"192.0.2.14","src_port":39100,"dest_ip":"10.0.1.22","dest_port":22,"proto":"TCP","alert":{"action":"allowed","gid":1,"signature_id":2001219,"signature":"ET SCAN Potential SSH Scan","category":"Attempted Information Leak","severity":3}}
commonPitfalls: Suricata EVE JSON files can also contain non-alert records (dns, flow, stats). Filter for event_type == 'alert'.
Severity 1 alerts indicate active exploit execution and should trigger on-call pages.
productionTips: Use Vector or Fluent Bit to route severity 1 alerts directly to your SIEM while aggregating low-severity scan alerts.

title: Zeek (Bro) Network Security Monitoring Conn Log Parser
metaDescription: Parse Zeek / Bro conn.log network security session logs with connection durations, byte counters, and TCP state flags.

fields.name: ts
fields.description: Unix epoch timestamp with microsecond resolution.

fields.name: service
fields.description: Dynamically detected protocol service (ssl, http, dns) or '-'.

fields.name: orig_bytes
fields.description: Payload bytes sent by originator or '-'.

fields.name: resp_bytes
fields.description: Payload bytes sent by responder or '-'.

commonPitfalls: Zeek uses tab-delimited records (\t). Blank or unestablished sessions record duration and bytes as hyphens (-).
The uid field connects conn.log to http.log, ssl.log, and files.log for full transaction reconstruction.
productionTips: Alert on conn_state == 'REJ' or 'S0' from internal subnets to external public IPs as evidence of malware C2 beaconing.

title: Linux /var/log/auth.log & secure PAM Authentication Parser
metaDescription: Parse Linux authentication logs. Audit SSH logins, sudo escalations, invalid user attempts, and brute-force scans.
sampleLogs: Sep 26 23:30:00 bastion01 sshd[1420]: Accepted publickey for admin from 198.51.100.4 port 54210 ssh2
Sep 26 23:30:01 bastion01 sshd[1421]: Failed password for root from 203.0.113.88 port 48210 ssh2
Sep 26 23:30:02 bastion01 sshd[1422]: Failed password for invalid user test from 192.0.2.14 port 39100 ssh2
commonPitfalls: On RedHat/CentOS/Rocky Linux, authentication logs are stored in /var/log/secure; on Debian/Ubuntu, in /var/log/auth.log.
The phrase 'invalid user' appears only when the requested username does not exist on the system.
productionTips: Deploy Fail2ban or CrowdSec on bastion hosts to automatically block IP addresses generating more than 5 'Failed password' events in 60 seconds.
